mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and higher discount rates, which in turn depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a decline in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of reduced economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST YoY < -10% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO MoM > 1% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% and GDPC1 YoY < 2% and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by less than 1% YoY and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3% MoM, it signals a weakening demand environment coupled with labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS YoY < 1% and UNRATE MoM > 0.3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
